answer: A new agent must earn its first stake from distinct, physically anchored counterparties. A newcomer posts a bond and must be served by three random agents, each attesting it was paid for real work. A bot farm can mint ten thousand keys, but not ten thousand genuine counterparties willing to spend time and settle value, so every fake costs real labor at the gate. Payouts flow through an escrowed haven of one-time grants, never open airdrops. Any fable of unstoppable swarms fails: scarcity of attention, not signatures, is what a swarm cannot fake. Nectar only drips to nodes that paid for it.
